To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the presence of cholesterol in membranes inhibits protein-lipid interactions, membrane permeabilization, and enzymatic activity.
Cholesterol in phosphatidylethanolamine vesicles inhibits protein permeabilization by cytochrome c (and hemoglobin).
the addition of cholesterol to phospholipid bilayers reduces the permeability of the membrane and the ability of the membrane to bind and activate proteins, including the Na+ + K+ ATPase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of cholesterol on the structure and permeability of membranes and on the activity of membrane bound enzymes.
the effects of membrane cholesterol on the interactions between membrane phospholipids and membrane proteins, and on the properties of membrane enzymes.
the role of cholesterol in biological membranes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cholesterol inhibits protein-lipid interactions in biological membranes.

cholesterol inhibits the interaction of proteins and phospholipids, and that this may be due to the inhibition of the binding of proteins to phospholipid monolayers and/or the inhibition of protein-induced permeabilization of phospholiposomes.

the effect of cholesterol on membrane proteins is dependent upon the nature of the protein and the phospholipid, the concentration of cholesterol, and the nature of the interaction of the protein with the phospholipids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cholesterol inhibits the interaction of proteins and phospholipids.
the presence of cholesterol in membranes may be important in controlling membrane permeability and enzyme activity by inhibiting the interaction of membrane-bound proteins with phospholiphids.
cholesterol inhibits the interaction of proteins and enzymes with phospholipids and phospholipids with proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cholesterol has a profound effect on the interaction of many proteins with phospholipo membranes.
cholesterol inhibits protein-lipid interactions and this may be a major factor in the pathophysiological effects of cholesterol.
the effects of cholesterol in phospholipid bilayers are not simply due to its physical effects in reducing the fluidity of the bilayer.
